PullRequest.Title: sessions: add a More Actions menu to the Remote Environments header
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #349796.

In its default, ungrouped view, Remote Environments offered no way to add an environment: setup actions only appear on Type group headings or when nothing is found. That left no visible way to add an SSH host or to create a Dev Container on this computer. The Dev Tunnel sign-in was also hidden as soon as other environments were listed, so a fresh profile couldn't find its tunnels.

A **More Actions** button next to **Refresh** now offers:

- **Add SSH Host...**: enter `user@host[:port]`, choose how to authenticate and a name, then connect. Connecting saves the host, so it appears in the list. Unlike Connect via SSH in the environment picker, it doesn't ask for a folder or open a session. It runs a new command, `workbench.action.sessions.addSSHHost`, which isn't in the Command Palette because Connect to Remote Agent Host via SSH and Add New SSH Host... already are.
- **Create Dev Container...**: only while a Dev Container can be created, that is, the Dev Container setting is on and this computer or a connected host has Docker. It asks for the host when there's more than one.
- **Sign In to Dev Tunnels...**: only while finding tunnels needs sign-in. It uses the account provider that discovery asks for; choosing between GitHub and Microsoft stays with #349815.

WSL distributions, Dev Tunnels and GitHub Environments are discovered rather than added, so the menu offers nothing else for them.

`promptForCredentialsAndConnect` now returns the connected address, and the Connect via SSH flows ask for the folder themselves, so they behave as before. The accessibility help describes the new menu.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `node build/oxlint.ts` on the 7 changed TypeScript files: passed.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remotesWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostActions.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/electron-browser/remotesEditor.test.ts`: 250 passing. New tests cover the menu's items as availability changes and running each of them, and Add SSH Host connecting without asking for a folder or opening a session. Two layout tests now expect More Actions as the trailing header control.
- Not run: the component fixture screenshots. The new header button will likely change the Remote Environments screenshots.

Scenarios.Scenario: Construct, resize, and dispose Remote Environments; open the header More Actions menu or accessibility help.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget construction adds one ActionBar and dropdown control. Menu contents are requested only when the context menu opens; getAddActions reads two observable values and creates at most three actions plus a separator. Accessibility help remains generated on demand. No new discovery or connection work must finish before the menu opens.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One header control per widget, independent of environment count; at most three menu actions per opening. Existing table rendering and help generation retain their previous multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous bounded menu construction. ActionBar owns and disposes its view items; DropdownMenuActionViewItem registers its dropdown and hover resources. Both the added Action and ActionBar are registered with the widget.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Menu availability reads already-maintained observable state, not fresh Docker or authentication queries. Docker availability is cached per connector or remote connection, including negative results, in DevContainerEnvironments._updateEnvironmentHosts. Opening the menu does not invalidate or rerun those checks.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the lazy action-provider callback, constant-sized getAddActions implementation, unchanged render subscriptions, and disposal ownership were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling of the extra header control or changed flex layout; their cost is bounded and no changed repeated layout or collection-wide work was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: a bounded header control and on-demand menu are added without eager boundary calls, collection-scaling work, or lost cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add an SSH host from the new header action, including cold connection, cancellation, and adding an already-connected address.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Explicit user input and credential/name prompts precede connectWithProgress. A cold action awaits the existing SSH connection handshake before completing; it does not browse a remote folder or open a session. Connecting and retaining the saved host are the requested behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the shared-process SSH connect service for a cold address, then wait for the remote-agent connection handshake.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One underlying connection attempt per distinct cold SSH connection key; existing connected addresses bypass connectWithProgress's service call, and pending connections are joined by key in SSHRemoteAgentHostService.connect and the node service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This header route did not exist. Connect via SSH already used the same connection service once per cold address, followed by folder browsing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Connection readiness gates successful completion of this explicit action, not opening the header menu or listing other environments.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish SSH transport and execute the existing remote agent bootstrap/endpoint flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared SSH session per distinct connection key, with setup commands conditional on remote installation and endpoint state; repeated requests for the same pending key share the session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing Connect via SSH command established the same transport and ran the same bootstrap. The new command intentionally exposes that flow without its subsequent folder/session work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only after the user chooses to add and connect a host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the configured SSH entry before connecting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing registration update per cold action; no loop over discovered hosts is introduced. Entries remain intentionally owned by the remote-host service until forgotten.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connect via SSH persisted the same registration. The new route adds no extra copies or repeated persistence to that operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the existing connection setup path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit user actions and distinct SSH addresses, not the number of listed environments. Same-key pending attempts are coalesced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited action flow; independent addresses may connect concurrently as before. Same-address requests join existing work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connected addresses are reused. Renderer and node services join in-flight requests by connection key and remove pending entries after settlement. Cancellation during prompts issues no connection; failure cleanup and progress-listener disposal remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new action calls the unchanged credential/connection helper, with connected-address reuse and both renderer/node pending maps traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold SSH setup duration depends on authentication, network, and remote installation. No measurements were taken; no increased work per equivalent connection was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the expensive operation is an explicit, required connection, not speculative menu work or fan-out. The new route omits folder browsing and session creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the existing Connect via SSH flow for a manually entered host or an SSH alias requiring manual credentials.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Credential prompts await connectWithProgress, then the successful caller awaits promptForRemoteFolder. The refactor moves that existing folder prompt from the helper into each existing caller without adding another prompt or connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve an alias when applicable, and establish or reuse the existing SSH connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One alias resolution when an alias is selected, followed by at most one underlying connection attempt per cold key. Direct manual hosts skip alias resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same callers resolved aliases and invoked connectWithProgress once. The old helper then awaited the same folder prompt internally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution and handshake precede the folder picker, exactly as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the connected provider's existing browse action and open/select the chosen workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browse-action invocation per successful existing Connect via SSH flow, not one per provider or environment. Provider lookup is an in-memory search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: promptForCredentialsAndConnect invoked this same browse action once after a successful connection; the diff relocates the invocation to the caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Folder selection remains downstream of successful SSH connection and precedes selecting the workspace in a new session.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected SSH target and one folder picker per command; alias configuration lookup is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial prompts, connection, then folder browsing; the original ordering is preserved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The connected-address fast path and same-key in-flight coalescing are unchanged. The refactor does not invalidate connection or folder state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both modified callers and the removed helper-level folder invocation were compared directly in the diff.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Folder browsing duration depends on the remote provider and network, but the diff introduces no extra invocation or newly awaited expensive operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: equivalent before/after boundary-call counts and ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a Dev Container from the header when this computer or a connected host supports Docker.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The menu reads cached availability. On selection, the model builds the eligible-host picker, selects one host, revalidates it, and awaits createEnvironment for that host. The new environment is published before connection startup, keeping progress visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect one environment through the shared-process container service locally, or the chosen connected host's container-service protocol remotely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One environment connection flow for the selected host per explicit creation. Eligible-host count affects only in-memory picker construction, not the number of container-service calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing group, empty-state, and row Create Dev Container actions called the same model/service path. The header adds another route to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Container readiness gates completion of the explicit creation action; no container is created while merely opening the menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing Docker and devcontainer preparation/startup commands for the new environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A preparation/startup sequence per requested environment, conditional on image/container state; no command sequence per eligible host. Environment/source-key queues serialize operations for the same environment, not globally across independent environments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command sequence and per-key scheduling were reachable through existing creation controls; creating several environments concurrently was already supported.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited during explicit environment creation. Other rows and menu controls are not blocked waiting for all eligible hosts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare the environment-specific cache/configuration and Docker volume/container state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per explicitly created environment, keyed by its generated environment ID. No file preparation is triggered by evaluating menu availability.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing Create Dev Container routes prepared the same environment state and caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the existing explicit creation sequence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H eligible hosts for in-memory picker construction; C explicit creation requests produce C environments. The header does not create H containers or dispatch H boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-environment operation sequencing and pending-connect joining; independent environments can run concurrently. Neither the header route nor its availability evaluation introduces an automatic burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Host/Docker availability comes from existing positive/negative connection-scoped checks. The node service caches Docker executable resolution. Cold images may need Docker downloads; warm image/container state reuses existing Docker behavior. New environments intentionally have distinct IDs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the header callback, host selection, environment creation, per-state queue, connector dispatch, and node source-key queue were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Docker startup and image acquisition can be expensive, but command sequence, concurrency, and cache behavior are unchanged for equivalent requests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is an additional entry point to the existing explicitly requested creation flow, not new per-host fan-out or eager initialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial/explicit Remote Environments discovery and signing in to Dev Tunnels from the new header menu.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Displaying the widget still starts the existing discovery refresh. The new sign-in action first awaits authentication, then refreshes only if the widget remains visible and alive. Discovery refresh waits for four existing method tasks; other connection routes remain available and previous rows are preserved during refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request authentication createSession for the discovery-selected provider across the authentication extension-host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One interactive authentication request per explicit sign-in; the widget-wide signingInToTunnels guard rejects overlapping sign-in actions from any route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing row/empty-state sign-in actions used the same guarded signInToTunnels method and refresh sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authentication precedes post-sign-in discovery; it is not performed while opening the menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read SSH configuration and followed Include files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SSH inventory request per refresh, with Include traversal's existing visited set. Menu opening issues none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initial discovery, Refresh, and existing post-sign-in refresh read the same inventory once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The SSH discovery task must finish for the full refresh to settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve SSH aliases via ssh -G across the shared-process service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve IPC/subprocess per distinct alias after Set deduplication, limited to eight concurrent resolutions. No alias-resolution cache is added or invalidated by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deduplication, eight-wide limiter, and subprocess count were used by initial, explicit, and post-sign-in refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Alias resolution gates completion of the SSH discovery task, not connection through another method.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two concurrent WSL commands per refresh on Windows, independent of distribution count; no WSL discovery commands off Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two grouped probes were issued by the existing refresh path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The WSL task runs alongside the other discovery methods and contributes to full refresh completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve cached authentication, then enumerate supported tunnels through one shared-process list request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical inventory enumeration plus one sequential lookup per configured additional tunnel name; not one query per discovered tunnel. Without authentication, enumeration stops before the management-service call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing initial/explicit/post-sign-in refreshes issued the same grouped enumeration and additional-name lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the tunnel discovery task after sign-in. Cached authentication avoids interactive prompts during silent refresh, but refresh still enumerates tunnels.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List GitHub environments when the service is enabled and authenticated, then reconcile the returned inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical environment-list call per refresh, not one call per returned environment. Cold initialization is joined through the existing initialization promise. refresh:true bypasses the inventory cache, unchanged by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same list call, initialization joining, and forced-refresh cache behavior existed before the header route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in parallel with SSH, WSL, and tunnel discovery; full refresh awaits it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the local agent's active GitHub environment ID after inventory enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one optional local-ID read per GitHub-environment refresh, independent of inventory size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unchanged GitHub environment refresh already performed this read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of completing that discovery task.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct SSH aliases A, configured additional tunnel names N, and returned inventory sizes. Discovery launches four method tasks, SSH resolves at most eight aliases concurrently, WSL uses two probes total, and tunnel additional-name lookups are sequential.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Four method tasks in Promise.all, with SSH's eight-wide limiter, two parallel WSL probes, and sequential additional-tunnel-name requests. Sign-in remains guarded until its follow-up refresh settles. Existing refresh cancellation/version handling is preserved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The menu uses the recorded authentication-required state. Sign-in is coalesced by a widget-wide guard. Refresh uses cached authentication silently, preserves previous inventory on failed methods, deduplicates SSH aliases, and forces existing GitHub inventory refresh. Cancellation/version checks and refresh-button disabling are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new callback targets the same guarded sign-in method, and all discovery branches, grouped calls, cache behavior, and relevant limits were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh duration depends on alias count, configured tunnel names, subprocess latency, and network. Those costs are real but pre-existing; no increased call cardinality or altered concurrency was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new header exposes existing sign-in/discovery behavior without adding automatic refreshes, duplicate authentication requests, or additional collection-scaling boundary calls.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all eight changed files and every diff page; no binary or unreviewable patches. Compared added menu construction and disposal, explicit SSH addition, both refactored SSH callers, container creation, sign-in, discovery, layout, and on-demand help against the base behavior. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete performance-regression fix qualified. Static review only; no runtime profiling. The performance guide was requested but the host returned a truncated preview; learned-regression guidance was fully available.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
